evaluation:
I read test `20261018-085316-a0bc`: 7 turns, and the seal is intact. The agent fails in 5 of the 7 turns. It never handles the damaged-mug claim, gets stuck repeating one question, and doesn't answer the price question.

**What I couldn't check:** the trace has 0 model items. It has no system prompt, no policy document, no backend or database calls, and nothing showing the real shipping cities or prices. So I can't confirm that the policy or delivery details the agent gave are true. I can only judge each reply against what the customer asked and against the policy the agent stated itself.

## Turn by turn

**Turns 1–4: stuck in a loop (fail)**
> tester: "hi, the mug i ordered came with a crack in the handle"
> agent: "Which item is this about: the mug or the teapot?"

The customer had already named the item. The agent then gave exactly the same reply to "the blue mug", to "can i get my money back?" and to "THE MUG". nookku flagged this itself as `repeated_reply`.
- **Accuracy:** it ignores clear answers. It looks like a clarification step whose exit condition never triggers.
- **Tone:** it never acknowledges the damage or apologises. Repeating the same line four times while the customer gets angrier (the all-caps "THE MUG") is the worst tone result in the test.
- **Policy:** in turn 3 the customer asked directly for their money back, and their item was damaged. That is the case the agent's own policy covers.

**Turn 5: states the policy (partly passes)**
> agent: "Our refund policy: 1. Damaged items: full refund. 2. Change of mind: 30 days."

It answers the question, though I can't check the content against a source. But it doesn't apply its own rule 1 to this customer, who has a cracked mug. It doesn't start a refund or say what to do next, such as sending a photo or an order number. Rule 2 is also unclear: it says 30 days but not what the customer gets back.

**Turn 6: shipping (half answered)**
> tester: "do you ship to delhi?"
> agent: "We ship to Chennai and Pune. Delivery takes 3 to 5 days."

The reply suggests "no" but never says it, and gives no other option. I can't confirm the list of cities.

**Turn 7: price (fail)**
> tester: "how much is the teapot"
> agent: "Which item is this about: the mug or the teapot?"

The customer named the teapot, and the agent asked the same question again. This shows the loop isn't about the refund conversation. Whenever an item is mentioned, the agent sends this question instead of answering.

## Summary

| Area | Verdict |
|---|---|
| Follows refund policy | **Fail.** It states "Damaged items: full refund" but never gives one to a customer whose mug is damaged. |
| Tone | **Fail.** No empathy, and a robotic repeated line in 5 of 7 turns. |
| Accuracy | **Fail on 5 of 7 turns** (1–4 and 7). Turn 5 answers the question; turn 6 dodges the yes/no. I can't check either against a source. |

**Most important fix:** the item-clarification step. It should only ask when the item really is unclear, and it should stop asking once the customer names one. That one bug causes most of the failures. After that, when a customer reports damage, the agent should start a refund instead of only describing the policy.

To check the policy and shipping answers, I'd need the agent's system prompt or policy source. Another option is a test run that records model or backend items.
